MARKET.head: Australian wine stocks fall 9% to lowest level since 2019-20
MARKET.summ: The Australian wine industry produced less wine than it sold, helping reduce excess stock in 2025-26, according to Wine Australia’s latest Production, Sales and Inventory Report. The 2025-26 findings “indicate the sector has made progress in reducing stocks, but further adjustment is likely to be needed to move to a more...
takeaways: Wine Australia's report shows national wine inventory fell 9% in 2025-26 to 1.87 billion litres, the lowest since 2019-20.
Total wine production fell 18% to 925 million litres, while sales dropped 4% to 1.04 billion litres.
Wine Australia expects winegrape prices to stay below long-term averages for vintage 2027 as supply adjusts.

MARKET.head: French wine imports to China jump in September on restocking and cheaper 2024 Bordeaux
MARKET.summ: China’s imports of French wine surged in September 2026, with their value rising nearly 130% from August and volume almost doubling
takeaways: China imported 4.44 million litres of French wine worth US$73.69 million in September 2026, up 96.61% in volume from August.
Import value rose 129.70% month on month, pushing France ahead of Australia as China's largest wine source by value that month.
Importers credit year-end restocking and lower-priced 2024 Bordeaux, such as Carruades de Lafite, cut 25-41% from 2023 release prices.

MARKET.head: Changyu partners with South Korea's Ayoung as home profits slide
MARKET.summ: With profits down nearly 20% despite rising sales, Changyu has struck a deal with South Korean drinks group Ayoung to put its wines in supermarkets, specialist shops and restaurants and hired a local team to build demand beyond the first shipment
takeaways: China's Changyu, founded in Yantai in 1892, signed a strategic deal with South Korea's Ayoung Group for distribution and retail.
Changyu's nine-month 2026 revenue rose 6.51% to RMB 2.254 billion, but net profit fell 19.25% to RMB 151 million.
South Korea imported 27.07 million kilograms of wine worth US$214.78 million in first-half 2026, with volume down 3.18%.

MARKET.head: Fungus-resistant grape varieties cut Apulian table grape protection costs by 55%
MARKET.summ: Towards Sustainable Viticulture: Cost Savings and Reduced Chemical Use through Fungus-Resistant Grapevine Varieties
takeaways: Adopting fungus-resistant grapevine varieties in Apulian table grape production cuts plant protection costs by 55%.
Extended Gross Margins rise 7%, 8% with no drop in gross revenues, and cost variability also falls, per Galati et al. (2026).
The study appeared in Wine Economics and Policy.

MARKET.head: Sonoma regenerative vineyards match conventional returns over 30 years if yields hold
MARKET.summ: Economic viability of regenerative viticulture in Sonoma County, California IVES Technical Review adapted from Herrera et al. 2026
takeaways: A 30-year cost-benefit study compared regenerative and conventional management across four Sonoma County vineyards using a 2.5% discount rate.
Regenerative vineyards had slightly lower establishment costs but higher annual operating costs from compost and sheep grazing.
Returns came close to conventional farming when grape yields were maintained, with site fit and added grape value deciding success.

MARKET.head: Pridham calls for grower-led, regional collaboration to make Australian wine resilient
MARKET.summ: In the third instalment of his series examining the future of the Australian wine industry, Ben Pridham from Prodham Viticulture in McLaren Vale moves beyond the problems to consider what comes next. Drawing on his own business experience and examples from overseas, he makes the case for regional collaboration, grower-led...
takeaways: Ben Pridham of Pridham Viticulture in McLaren Vale argues Australia's wine industry should move from structures that squeeze growers to resilient, grower-led collaboration.
He cites Maggie Jarrett's Nuffield report, which found Griffith grape growers paid below cost of production, and Mendoza's region-by-region approach beating top-down San Juan.
South Australia's $109 million Wine Industry Transition and Growth Package includes a $100 million loan scheme to move unviable vineyards into higher-value uses.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux holds 41% of fine wine trade as Burgundy share climbs
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux claimed 35.7% of traded value. Burgundy and Champagne followed closely behind
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded fine wine value, with 2019 and 2020 vintages top-traded by value.
Burgundy's share of traded value rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6%, led by Soldera Case Basse and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: Burgundy's top estates face tight supply and allocation squeezes in China
MARKET.summ: Some of Burgundy’s most sought-after wines are becoming harder to source in China, importers told Vino Joy News, as smaller harvests and tighter allocations constrain supply
takeaways: Importers say supplies of DRC, Leroy, Leflaive and Gros Frère et Sœur tightened from July, with Leflaive's entry-level whites selling out.
Fine West's Wu says Leflaive produced less in 2024 and 2025 and cut allocations to China, so shortages reflect supply, not higher consumption.
Other merchants, including Shanghai Boyun's Lin, report steady supply and falling prices, so accounts of shortage remain disputed.

MARKET.head: English sparkling wine expands plantings but faces oversupply and falling grape prices
MARKET.summ: After a decade of rapid growth and rising international recognition, English sparkling wine faces the challenge of turning enthusiasm into sustained sales
takeaways: Wines of Great Britain's 2025 report says English vine plantings rose 510 percent from 2005 to 2024, to 4,841 hectares.
Global exports of English wine rose 35 percent from 2023 to 2024, with the US among leading markets for producers like Gusbourne.
Grape prices fell about 50 percent after the large 2023 vintage left wineries overstocked, reaching historic lows by end of 2025.

MARKET.head: Sustainability information lifts consumer willingness to pay for PIWI wine
MARKET.summ: The Effect of Sustainability Information on Consumers' Preferences for Fungus-Resistant Grape Wine
takeaways: A study tested how sustainability information affects consumer preferences for wine made from fungus-resistant (PIWI) grapes.
Its authors argue wineries should communicate sustainability clearly to move PIWI wines beyond a small niche market.

MARKET.head: Guangdong lychee ice wine sells out online after APEC dinner menu circulates
MARKET.summ: A Guangdong lychee wine became an unexpected online hit after it was served alongside two Changyu wines at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen, with its producer reporting a more than 93,000% jump in revenue at one online store
takeaways: Yueli Lychee Ice Wine, made by Guangzhou ShunChangYuan in Conghua, was served at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen.
After the November 18 menu circulated online, one Tmall flagship store logged about 5,000 orders in two hours.
The producer reported a 93,393.10% revenue jump at one online store, without stating the comparison period.

MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under Leo Wang
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite appointed former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang as managing director of Domaine de Long Dai and China market.
The move puts the Shandong winery and national sales team under one leader for the first time.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, at the estate nine years, leaves at year end.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie for North American marketing
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission appointed Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico and Central America.
She previously served as CEO of the Center for Produce Safety and as international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
Her role is to expand promotional opportunities and increase demand for fresh California table grapes in those markets.

CULTURE.head: Mandoon Estate wins 32 trophies and 47 gold medals in 2026
CULTURE.summ: Swan Valley winery Mandoon Estate is celebrating an “extraordinary year of success on the Australian wine show circuit”, collecting a total of 32 trophies and 47 gold medals in 2026. Significantly, Mandoon Estate was named Most Successful Exhibitor at three of Western Australia's major wine shows , the Swan Valley Wine Show,...
takeaways: Swan Valley winery Mandoon Estate collected 32 trophies and 47 gold medals across Australian wine shows in 2026.
Mandoon was named Most Successful Exhibitor at the Swan Valley, Margaret River and Wine Show of Western Australia shows.
Its 2018 Reserve Sparkling won the Dr Tony Jordan Trophy for Best Sparkling at the 2026 Melbourne Royal Wine Awards.

CULTURE.head: AWRI re-elects two directors and appoints Steven Weinert to its board
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Wine Research Institute (AWRI) has announced the re-election of Corrina Wright and Brett McClen to its board as well as the appointment of Steven Weinert as a director. Voted by wine grapes levy payers, Corrina Wright was re-elected in the ‘small wine grapes levy payer’ category (up to 2,000 tonnes) and Brett...
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute announced re-elections of Corrina Wright and Brett McClen as directors, both starting 1 January 2027.
Steven Weinert, a former Pernod Ricard and Wine Australia executive, was appointed director from 1 November 2026 and will chair the audit committee.
Trish Giannini and Sarah Courtney left the board on 31 October 2026, Courtney after Liberal Party preselection for the Australian Senate.

CULTURE.head: VinePair names 20 Proseccos to buy in 2026, tasted without blind conditions
CULTURE.summ: Prosecco continues to be a bright spot for the wine industry, as the Italian sparkling wine manages to keep growing year after year. Between the thirst for affordable bubbly and the unstoppable rise of the Spritz category, it’s no wonder more consumers are looking to this budget-friendly style. Even though the standard DOC...
takeaways: VinePair's tasting panel scored submitted Proseccos on a 100-point scale for aromas, flavors, texture and finish.
Producers sent samples free of charge, and tastings were not blind, with producer and price known.
The list of 20 bottles is meant to help drinkers buy affordable Prosecco, with a Prosecco Rosé designation added in 2020.

CULTURE.head: ProWine Shanghai shows China's wine buyers seeking distinctive, regional, casual-occasion wines
CULTURE.summ: China’s wine market is becoming more selective, more diverse and less dependent on formal drinking occasions, according to exhibitors at this year’s ProWine Shanghai
takeaways: Exhibitors at ProWine Shanghai say Chinese buyers are becoming more selective, seeking wines with distinctive character beyond quality and price.
The three-day exhibition drew over 620 exhibitors from 34 countries and regions and 21,800 trade visitors this year.
Wine is increasingly drunk at smaller gatherings, casual restaurants, wine bars and at home, not only business banquets and gifting.

CULTURE.head: Ten new booze books for holiday gifting, covering spirits, wine, tea and beer
CULTURE.summ: Buying gifts for your friends and family every holiday season can be overwhelming. Luckily, avid drinks enthusiasts make it a bit easier to cater to their interests. While the go-to might be a baller bottle of Burgundy or an esoteric bourbon, books are a simple, personal, and effective gift to deepen their knowledge of beverages.
takeaways: Ten booze books selected as holiday gifts, ranging from cocktail manuals to historical accounts.
Picks include a 400-year history of Chartreuse by Jordan Mackay and Paul Einbund.
Also featured: Robert Simonson on American whiskey cocktails, and Nick Rowan's guide to Japanese wine regions.

SCIENCE.head: Sustainable Wine Reference Group benchmarks 40+ standards, reveals gaps and design differences
SCIENCE.summ: (5 min read) Over the past three years, SWR has embarked on the mammoth process of benchmarking the more than 40 sustainability standards that exist globally in wine. Mammoth because the documentation of a standard can easily surpass 1500 pages of documents. The rationale for this when we started was simple.
takeaways: Sustainable wine body SWR spent three years benchmarking more than 40 global sustainability standards for wine.
Its Global Reference Framework scores standards across 39 topics, and the OIV now uses it to revise its wine sustainability definition.
Packaging and logistics are the widest gap, while some standards treat labour issues as matters for national law.

SCIENCE.head: Biochar in vineyard soils: review weighs yield gains and carbon storage
SCIENCE.summ: The use of biochar in agricultural soils: Impacts on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration
takeaways: Leonel J.R. Nunes published a study on biochar use in vineyard soils in Science of The Total Environment in November 2026.
The paper assesses effects of biochar on vineyard productivity and its potential for carbon capture and sequestration.

SCIENCE.head: Review ranks tools for grapevine resilience under dry-farming water stress
SCIENCE.summ: The study provides a narrative and critical literature review evaluating the physiological, agronomic, and practical tools available to enhance vineyard resilience under dry-farming conditions, and analyzes grapevine strategies for managing water stress. Published by Poni et al 2026 in Agronomy, MDPI Headline Findings Results
takeaways: Poni et al. published a narrative and critical review in MDPI's Agronomy journal in 2026.
The review evaluates physiological and agronomic tools that could make dry-farmed vineyards more resilient to water stress.
It also analyses grapevine strategies for managing water stress under rising temperatures and erratic rainfall.

SCIENCE.head: Winter cover crops plus foliar biostimulant match tilled Syrah yields in Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Pairing winter-spring cover crops with a foliar nitrogen-fixing microbial biostimulant supports sustainable rainfed viticulture through complementary soil and plant pathways, boosting soil nutrient enzymes while keeping yields and juice traits competitive or improved
takeaways: A 2020-2021 rainfed organic Syrah trial in southern Spain compared tillage with winter-spring cover crops across three foliar Methylobacterium biostimulant doses.
Cover crops raised soil nutrient enzyme activity and decomposition potential across the 48 focal vines studied.
High-dose biostimulant combined with cover crops matched or beat tilled yields and suggested synergy in juice Brix and pH, published March 2027.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Rogovila - Wine is Culture
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Celebrating Slovenian garagiste David Bratož, plus the domaine's new releases
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: David Bratož, founder of Rogovila in Slovenia's Vipava Valley, died in November 2025 after falling ill with leukaemia.
Rogovila produces around 4,000 bottles a year from half a hectare of old vines inherited in 1999, bottling its first official vintage in 2021.
After his death, daughter Lana, who keeps a full-time office job in Nova Gorica, continues the winery with help from her mother and two sisters.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Schloss Vaux: this leading German sparkling wine house has a new home on the Rhein
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I visited Vaux, one of Germany’s leading sparkling wine houses, in August 2026. They took a group of press to
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Schloss Vaux has opened VAUX am Rhein, a new visitor venue in Eltville's 12th-century Crass fortress, led by sommelier Florian Richter.
Vaux, founded in Berlin in 1868, produces about 450,000 bottles of traditional-method sparkling wine annually.
Vaux sources fruit from its own vineyards, planted since 2014, plus the Rheingau, Pfalz and Nahe, and has no reserve wine programme.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Auction: The Drama, the Records and the Wines That Found Their Buyers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the drama and record-breaking moments from this iconic Burgundy charity wine auction, featuring exceptional barrels and the buyers who claimed them
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 166th Hospices de Beaune auction on 15 November raised €14.4 million at the hammer, down from €18.8 million last year.
Red barrels averaged €28,931, up 5 per cent, while white barrels averaged €39,893, down from €58,580 as white Burgundy prices corrected.
The Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru charity barrel sold for €770,000 to Alaor Pereira Lino of Anima Vinum, with Faiveley adding €230,000 for a €1 million total.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/22/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Beaujolais producers like Georges Duboeuf began marketing Beaujolais Nouveau beyond France in the 1970s with the slogan "Le Beaujolais Nouveau est arrivé!".
Natural winemakers Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Pierre-Marie Chermette made Beaujolais in the 1970s and 1980s using sustainable farming and minimal intervention.
Lapierre in Morgon labels its new red as Vin de France with the nickname "Raisins Gaulois", because cru wines cannot carry the Beaujolais Nouveau label.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast named California's Livermore Valley its 2026 American Wine Region of the Year in its annual Wine Star Awards.
Livermore's regional association named Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.
A Cabernet Franc claimed top honours at Maryland's Governor's Cup, per the Cab Franc Chronicles roundup.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, Champagne's black grapes, have colourless juice, so they can make white 'Blanc de Noirs' Champagne.
Teinturier grapes have red flesh; Garnacha Tintorera (Alicante Bouschet) was bred in 19th-century France, partly because deeply coloured wines fetched more money.
The featured Pago Casa Gran 'Reposo' 2024 from Valencia, Spain is a blend of 60% Garnacha Tintorera, 20% Syrah and 20% Monastrell.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics are judged by expertise, but the right level is 'a tad more' than the target audience's own knowledge.
Atkin says the American critic model favours tasting ability while the British model favours theoretical knowledge and scholarship.
Atkin criticises wine reviewers spending only about 30 seconds per wine, comparing it to reviewing a movie from its trailer.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources such as local-language catalogues, merchant inventory, auction notices, and private cellar consignments.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or images, and Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is available and connects them with the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with a Guangzhou stop set for November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but only a quarter of leader Australia.
Spain ranked sixth for value in China, with DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo cited as entry-level options around RMB12 to RMB24.
